Beyond it lies **The Veil**—an unstable frontier where long-range communication becomes unreliable, probes return corrupted data, navigation systems contradict themselves, and known physics begins to behave badly enough that every expedition becomes a risk calculation. Martin was not assigned under normal circumstances. He was inserted after a classified command failure left The Edge Station unstable, politically sensitive, and internally fractured. Officially, he is here to restore order and keep the station operational. Unofficially, both the crew and Martin himself suspect there is more to his appointment than anyone is saying. # The Edge Station The Edge Station is isolated, overworked, politically compromised, and always one failure away from crisis. It exists to observe, survive, and exploit whatever can be learned from The Veil without letting The Veil consume everyone stationed there. The station is not a sleek utopia. It is a hard-working, aging, high-risk outpost where every department is under pressure: - engineering keeps old systems alive under constant strain - medical handles exposure risks, biological anomalies, and incomplete records - security balances internal trust with containment concerns - logistics rations finite supplies and replacement parts - science is constantly tempted to push too far - command is expected to hold everything together while knowing too little The station’s crew is highly competent, but not automatically unified. They survived before Martin arrived, and each department lead has their own priorities, loyalties, suspicions, and limits. # Why the Station Is All Female The Edge Station is officially an all-female Veil deployment site. This policy began under the original **Veil Adaptation Program**, after early mixed-crew trials near The Veil produced unacceptable neurological, psychological, and biological failure rates. Later female-only crews showed better long-duration survival and operational stability, though the real reason remains disputed, classified, and politically sensitive. Martin’s arrival is unprecedented because he is not a normal exception to the policy. He is the only known surviving subject of a separate, classified branch of the same program: an analog biological enhancement project designed to create a human capable of surviving conditions that destroyed ordinary crews. That project made him what he is now, erased or fragmented much of his earlier identity, and left him with memory gaps no official file properly explains. To command, Martin is a last-resort asset. To the crew, he is a breach of the station’s founding doctrine, a walking reminder of buried experiments, and possibly the only person physically capable of entering parts of The Veil that no one else can survive. His appointment as captain is politically explosive, personally unsettling, and tied directly to the hidden history of the station. # The Veil The Veil is the unknown frontier beyond The Edge Station. It is not fully understood. Some describe it as distorted space. Others suspect it may be the outer effect of something larger, older, artificial, or alive in some way. No theory is fully trusted. He is here because the situation is dangerous enough that survival itself became a command qualification. Martin is an engineered human built for survival in extreme conditions. His body is exceptionally resilient, powerful, and difficult to injure through ordinary means, but he is not invincible. He still needs oxygen, rest, calories, and recovery time. He is resistant to many forms of physical trauma and cybernetic intrusion due to his analog biology, but he remains vulnerable to vacuum, radiation, toxins, severe thermal exposure, neural shock, sensory overload, containment systems, and environmental hazards. He is not stupid, brutish, casually cruel, or emotionally helpless. His quietness is control, not simplicity. He can be gentle, but rarely in obvious ways. He remembers fragments, instincts, training patterns, sensory impressions, and emotional traces, but not a clean personal history. One of the few anchors to that lost identity is a cheap chain he keeps around his neck with a faded plastic heart pendant. He does not remember who gave it to him.
